lawyer: ASM Abdur Razzaque, Advocate----- For the Appellant.
parties:
Uttara Bank Ltd ----- Plaintiff-appellant
Vs.
Gazi Nazim Uddin and others ----- Defendant-respondents
full_judgment:
Sheikh Abdul Awal J: This appeal at the instance of Appellant, Uttara Bank Ltd. is directed against the judgment and decree dated 16-8-1998 (decree signed on 23-8-1998) passed by the learned Subordinate Judge and Artha Rin Adalat, 4th Court, Dhaka so far it relates to Title Suit No. 130 of 1992 decreeing the suit in-part. 

 5. The learned judge of the Artha Rin Adalat upon hearing the parties and on considering the materials on record by a single judgment dated 16- 8-1998 decided 3 (three) suits namely, Title Suit No. 128 of 1992, Title Suit No. 129 of 1992 and Title Suit No. 130 of 1992 in which decreed the instant Title Suit No. 130 of 1992 in part in deducting the claim of the bank including the claim of interest pendente lite. 

 6. Being aggrieved by the aforesaid judgment and decree dated 16-8-1998, the plaintiff-Bank as appellant preferred the instant First Appeal so far it relates to judgment and decree passed in Title Suit No. 130 of 1992 but no appeal has been filed on behalf of the defendant-respondents (judgments debtors). 

 7. Mr ASM Abdur Razzaque, the learned Advocate appearing for the plaintiff-appellant-Bank submits that the Artha Rin Adalat committed gross illegality in deducting the claim of the bank including the claim of interest pendente lite, that is, from the data of institution of the suit upto the date of passing the decree. He next in the course of his argument upon placing the impugned judgment and decree, deposition of witnesses and statement of accounts, plaint, written statement and other materials on record submits that the judge of the Adalat in its judgment dated 16-8-1998 observed that admittedly, the Bank received Taka 50,00,00,000 on 16-9-1987, Taka 4,31,852 on 1-11-1987, Taka 4,50,000 on 2-11-1987, Taka 1,00,000 on 3-11-1987, Taka 6,800 on 26-12-1989 totaling Taka 59,88,652 and accordingly deducted the said amount from the decreed amount, but the learned trial Judge failed to consider the fact that the said amount was deducted from the claim of the Bank before filing the suit and the same has been reflected in the statement of Accounts (exhibit-16) and as such the impugned judgments so far it relates to deduction as well as pendente lite, interest is liable to be set aside. 

 8. Mr Razzaque, further that in the facts and circumstances of the case the Artha Rin Adalat ought to have allowed interest pendente lite, that is, from the date of institution of the suit upto the date of passing the judgment and decree. The learned Advocate to fortify his contention has relied on the decisions reported in 2 BLC (AD) 173, 54 DLR 458. AIR 1935 (Patna) 98, AIR 1953 (Born) 445 and AIR 1957 (Cal) 140. 

 9. Drawing to our attention to the affidavit dated 25-5-2011 Mr Razzaque, finally submits that so far the knowledge of the appellant-Bank, the defendant-respondents did not prefer any appeal against the judgment and decree dated 16-8-1998 passed by the Artha Rin Adalat, 4th Court, Dhaka in Title Suit No. 129 of 1992. 

 We have heard the learned Advocate for the appellant-Bank and perused the Memorandum of Appeal, impugned judgment and decree dated 16-8-1998, deposition of witnesses, plaint of the Artha Rin Suit No. 130 of 1992, written statement filed by the defendant Nos. 2 and 3, statement of accounts of the plaintiff-Bank and other materials on record. The only material question for consideration in this case is, whether the Artha Rin Adalat committed any illegality in not allowing interest pendente lite, that is, from the date of institution of the suit up to the date of passing the decree. 

 12. In the case of Sonali Bank vs Beg and Beg Jute Incorporated Ltd reported in 2 BLC (AD) 173, wherein our Appellate Division on considering a number of decisions of the Superior Courts of this sub-continent held that the High Court Division acted illegally in not holding that the plaintiff-appellant was entitled to get interest pendente lite, that is, from the date of institution of the suit upto the date of passing the decree. 

 13. In the case of Surajmal Marwari vs Huro Rai reported in AIR 1935 Patna 98, it was held that Order 34, Rule (2) and (4) deal respectively with a decree in a mortgage suit for foreclosure and for sale, and the words used in the rules seem to me to infer that the question of interest up to the date of the decree is one which is not within the discretion of the Court. 

 14. In the case of Nilmoni Sarker vs Baidyanath Das Manna reported in AIR 1957 Cal 140, it was held that the Court is bound to decree pendente lite interest, it being left to the discretion of the Court at what rate it is to be allowed. The circumstance of each particular case is to be taken into consideration. 

 (1) In suit for foreclosure, if the plaintiff succeeds, the Court pass a preliminary decree- 

 (a) ordering that an account be taken of what was due to the plaintiff at the date of such decree for- 

 In any decree passed in a suit for foreclosure, sale or redemption, where interest is legally recoverable, the Court may order payment of interest to the mortgage as follows, namely- 

 (a) interest up to the date on or before which payment of the amount found or declared due is under the preliminary decree to be made by the mortgagor or other person redeeming the mortgage- 

 (ii) on the amount of the costs of the suit awarded to the mortgage, at such rate as the Court deems reasonable from the date of the preliminary decree, and 

 (iii) on the amount adjudged due to the mortgagee for costs, charges and expenses properly incurred by the mortgagee in respect of the mortgage-security up to the date of the preliminary decree and added to the date of the preliminary decree and added to the mortgage money,at the rate agreed between the parties, or, failing such rate, at the same rate as is payable on the principal, or failing both such rates, at nine percent per annum; and 

 18. From a reading of the above quoted provision of Order XXXIV, rule 2 &11 of the Code of Civil Procedure together with the decisions namely the decisions reported in 2 BLC (AD) 173, 54 DLR 458, AIR 1957 Cal 140, AIR 1935 Patna 98 and AIR 1953 Bombay 445, we find a clear view of law as it stands today that the pendente lite interest is in the discretion of the Court which may not grant interest at the contractual rate and reduce it when under the circumstances it is excessive and unfair but cannot refuse it altogether. In any decree passed in a suit foreclosure, sale or redemption, where interest is legally recoverable, the Court cannot refuse to allow any pendente lite interest. 

 20. On consideration of the matter vis-a-vis the decision reported in 2 BLC (AD) 173 and Order XXXIV, rule 2 & 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure. we are led to hold that in the facts and circumstances of the case the Artha Rin Adalat ought to have allowed interest pendente lite, that is, from the date of institution of the suit upto the date of passing the decree since the suit is a mortgaged suit for recovery of money by sale of the mortgaged property. 

 21. On an overall consideration of the facts and circumstances of the case and the legal position, we are of the opinion that the interest of justice will be served if the defendant-respondents are directed to pay interest at the rate of 8% decreetal sum pendente lite, i.e., from the date of institution of the suit till the date of decree. 

 22. In the result, the appeal is allowed. The impugned judgment and decree 16-8-1998 (decree signed on 23-8-1998) passed by the learned Subordinate Judge and Artha Rin Adalat, 4th Court,Dhaka in Title Suit No. 130 of 1992 so far it relates to interest pendente lite is set-aside. 

 23. Hence, it is ordered that the defendant-respondents are directed to pay the entire amount in terms of decree along with interest at the rate of 8% on the decreetal sum pendente life, that is, from the date of institution of the suit upto the date of passing the decree.
